page_note: This page is dominated by a pastoral/sapiential parable teaching about Wisdom (Sophia) and her reception by hearers. The page opens with a natural-correspondence description (fire hidden in wood revealed when kindled) which is substrate-like in voice. This is then applied analogically to Wisdom in the heart of man — a sapiential/pastoral application, not a cosmological mapping. A clear dialogue frame (segs 11-12, 18) introduces a disciple's pastoral question (why do some receive Wisdom and others not?) and the apostle's parabolic answer (Wisdom is like a youth brought forth from a woman: kin rejoice, strangers grieve). The content is similitude addressed to the audience-situation — second side of the mapping points to contemporary teaching reception, not to cosmic registers. Substrate is thin; the page is mostly dialogue frame + hortatory/sapiential application built on a kernel of natural correspondence.
